title: Pandas Dates and Time-Series Fundamentals
learningObjectives: Explain the purpose of pandas dates and time-series fundamentals.
Choose Pandas APIs and parameters that match the input structure.
Apply the operations to deterministic Series and DataFrames.
Validate output shape, schema, data types and missing values.
Recognize edge cases and data-quality risks.

understand.concept: Pandas provides datetime-aware values and indexes for time-series work. to_datetime parses date-like input, date_range creates regular timestamps, and resample groups observations into time bins. Time-zone assumptions, sorting and frequency choices matter; resampling requires a datetime-like index.
understand.whyItMatters: Reliable data workflows ingest, combine, analyze and publish structured information. Correct parsing and transformations prevent silent data loss and misleading conclusions.
understand.analogy: A DataFrame workflow is like organizing labeled records: labels and matching rules determine how records are connected.
understand.summary: Pandas provides datetime-aware values and indexes for time-series work. to_datetime parses date-like input, date_range creates regular timestamps, and resample groups observations into time bins. Time-zone assumptions, sorting and frequency choices matter; resampling requires a datetime-like index.

explain.narrative: This lesson explores pandas dates and time-series fundamentals with small reproducible datasets. Inspect input structure before selecting parsing, join, time-frequency or export options. Validate resulting columns, row counts, index, dtypes and missing values. examples.title: Extract date parts
examples.code:
import pandas as pd
d=pd.to_datetime(['2026-02-14'])
print(d.month[0],d.day[0])

examples.title: Monthly resampling
examples.code:
import pandas as pd
i=pd.to_datetime(['2026-01-01','2026-01-02','2026-02-01'])
s=pd.Series([2,3,5],index=i)
print(s.resample('MS').sum().tolist())
